summary.title: A mechanism for pi phase shifts in Little-Parks experiments: application to 4Hb-TaS2 and to 2H-TaS2 intercalated with chiral molecules
summary.objective: To propose an alternative, conventional explanation for the observed pi phase shifts in Little-Parks experiments on 4Hb-TaS2 and chiral molecule-intercalated 2H-TaS2 without requiring unconventional or exotic pairing mechanisms.
summary.problem: Recent Little-Parks experiments on layered superconductor descendants of 2H-TaS2 (specifically 4Hb-TaS2 and chiral molecule-intercalated 2H-TaS2) reported unusual pi phase shifts, which were previously interpreted as evidence of exotic chiral or multi-component superconductivity. However, these interpretations conflict with the observation of robust transition temperatures and disorder tolerance.
summary.methodology: Extend Kulik's theory of Josephson coupling through a tunneling barrier containing paramagnetic impurities by incorporating strong Ising-type spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and spin-momentum locking in single 1H-TaS2 layers. Analyze the effects of lattice defects like screw dislocations on layered superconducting rings.
summary.results: Demonstrated that Ising spin-momentum locking strongly suppresses spin-independent (normal) interlayer tunneling while spin-flip tunneling due to paramagnetic impurities remains robust, leading to a negative Josephson coupling (J < 0). Combined with screw dislocations or stacking faults, this negative coupling naturally generates pi phase shifts in Little-Parks experiments for about half of the samples.
summary.limitations: The precise microscopic origin of spin-flip scattering in the molecular intercalation case requires further understanding, though local moments near the molecule-TaS2 interface are plausible.
summary.future_work: Directly detect the presence or absence of the pi phase in the Josephson coupling using vertical SQUID measurements.
